name: Brisbane
tagline: A laid-back river city of parks, galleries and koalas, with warm weather all year
description: Brisbane is Queensland's capital, a leafy river city built around the loops of the Brisbane River. The South Bank Parklands, City Botanic Gardens and the cultural precinct make it easy to wander on foot. Its museums, galleries and Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary cover art, history and wildlife, and Mount Coot-tha looks out over the city.
whyVisit: Ride a CityCat along the river

goodToKnow.title: Get a go card
goodToKnow.detail: The go card covers trains, buses, ferries and trams across Brisbane at cheaper fares than paper tickets. It needs a $10 deposit and is sold at stations and shops.

goodToKnow.title: Sun and storms
goodToKnow.detail: Summer is hot and humid with afternoon storms, so bring sun protection and plan outdoor sights for the morning.

goodToKnow.title: Use the river
goodToKnow.detail: CityCat and ferry services run along the river and are a cheap way to reach South Bank, New Farm and other riverside stops.

bestTimeBlurb: Mild, dry weather from {months} suits walking and outdoor dining. Summer is hot, humid and stormy.

name: Gold Coast
tagline: Surf beaches, theme parks and a glitzy skyline on a warm subtropical coast
description: The Gold Coast is a long strip of ocean beaches in Queensland's south-east corner, with more than 50 km of patrolled sand. Surfers Paradise is the high-rise hub of tourist activity, while Burleigh Heads and Currumbin have a quieter, local feel. Theme parks, wildlife sanctuaries and a mild, sunny climate fill out a visit. Rainforest-covered hills sit just inland.
whyVisit: Surf and swim the patrolled beaches

goodToKnow.title: Swim between the flags
goodToKnow.detail: Almost all beaches from the Seaway to Coolangatta are patrolled. Swim between the red and yellow flags and escape a rip by swimming parallel to shore.

goodToKnow.title: Tram and train links
goodToKnow.detail: A light-rail line runs along the coast through Surfers Paradise, and a train links the Gold Coast with Brisbane, so a car is optional.

goodToKnow.title: Book park tickets ahead
goodToKnow.detail: The big theme parks are spread across the northern suburbs and can be cheaper online. Plan one park per day.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring sunny days, warm seas and fewer crowds. Summer brings storms.
unverified: Tram and train links, ticket-booking advice are from general knowledge, not read on the Wikivoyage page in this run

name: Gold Coast Hinterland
tagline: Rainforest waterfalls and mountain lookouts just behind the Gold Coast's high-rises
description: The Gold Coast Hinterland is the rural area west of the Gold Coast, made up of mountain ranges covered in rainforest, most of it national park. Walking tracks lead to waterfalls such as Purling Brook Falls, Coomera Falls and Morans Falls. Lookouts across the coast and the Numinbah Valley, and the long-distance Gold Coast Hinterland Great Walk, add more reasons to leave the beach.
whyVisit: Take in lookouts over the coast
Hike the Great Walk through rainforest

goodToKnow.title: A car is far easier
goodToKnow.detail: Public transport west of the M1 is very sparse, so drive or join a tour from the coast.

goodToKnow.title: Slippery tracks after rain
goodToKnow.detail: Waterfall tracks can be wet and slippery. Wear sturdy shoes and stay behind barriers.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} are mild enough for long walks, and waterfalls still run after summer rain.

name: Scenic Rim
tagline: Volcanic peaks, rainforest parks and farm country an hour from Brisbane
description: The Scenic Rim is a rural region in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range, an hour south of Brisbane and inland from the Gold Coast. It holds more than 30,000 hectares of parkland, including World Heritage listed Gondwana Rainforests parks. Peaks such as Mount Barney and Mount Maroon draw walkers, while Lake Moogerah, Queen Mary Falls and Spicers Gap add lookouts, water and farm-gate stops.
whyVisit: Climb rugged peaks like Mount Barney
Look out from mountain gaps and lakes

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: Transport into the Scenic Rim is very limited. Most roads beyond the Mount Lindesay Highway are narrow, so allow extra drive time.

goodToKnow.title: Peaks are for experienced walkers
goodToKnow.detail: Mount Barney and Mount Maroon are steep, rocky climbs. Go early, carry water and check conditions first.

bestTimeBlurb: Cooler, drier weather from {months} is best for climbing and bushwalking. Summer brings heat and storms.
unverified: Peak difficulty and seasonal advice are general guidance not on the Wikivoyage page

name: Moreton Island
tagline: A sand island of dunes, shipwreck snorkelling and whales off Brisbane
description: Moreton Island is a sand island 36 km long that lies 35 km off Brisbane, and 98% of it is national park. Visitors go for the Tangalooma Wrecks, a cluster of sunken ships that form an artificial reef, and for freshwater lakes, giant dunes and a long surf beach. Cape Moreton has the state's oldest lighthouse, and humpback whales pass offshore on their annual migration.

goodToKnow.title: Ferries run from Brisbane
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle and passenger ferries leave the Brisbane River daily in peak periods, and the resort runs passenger services from Pinkenba.

goodToKnow.title: 4WD and permits needed
goodToKnow.detail: Only 4WD vehicles can drive the island and each needs a vehicle access permit. Camping needs a permit booked before you arrive.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the best time for humpback whales and mild, dry days on the sand.
